column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/auto-bump.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran
# cargo-auto-release. The run reported SUCCESS: `bump` bumped, tagged and
# pushed; `ship` was SKIPPED; nothing was published; nothing said so. The
# condition doing the skipping was correct — the failure was that nobody had
# written down WHICH JOBS MUST RUN for a given input, so a deliberate skip and
# a broken skip produced the same green tick. These rows are that missing
# statement for auto-bump.
# WHAT auto-bump IS. Substrate's self-bump: every push to main tags the repo so
# consumers of its reusable workflows can pin a revision instead of floating on
# @main. One job, `bump`, and exactly one axis in its `if:` —
#   if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'
# That single guard is the LOOP BRAKE. `bump`'s last step pushes a tag as
# github-actions[bot]; without the guard the resulting push re-enters this
# workflow and tags again, forever. Rows 1-2 are the two arms of that guard and
# are the only rows here that assert anything a condition actually reads.
# WHY THE NEAR-MISS ROWS (3-5) ARE NOT PADDING. The guard is an exact-string
# `!=` against one login, so it is a WHITELIST OF ONE FAILURE. Every other
# identity — a human, another bot, or no actor at all — falls through to
# "run". Rows 3-5 pin that fall-through in the three shapes most likely to
# change under someone's fingers:
#   - `github-actions` without the `[bot]` suffix, the login people write from
#     memory. If the literal in the workflow is ever "corrected" to the bare
#     form, row 4 goes NOT-RUN and the loop brake is proven unhooked BEFORE it
#     is a runaway tag loop in production.
#   - `dependabot[bot]`, a second bot that legitimately pushes to main. It must
#     still get a tag; the brake is scoped to the bot this workflow itself
#     creates, not to bots in general. If the guard is ever widened to
#     `!endsWith(github.actor, '[bot]')` — or to any construct at all — row 5
#     turns NOT-RUN or EVAL and the widening lands as a decision.
#   - the EMPTY actor. GitHub yields empty for an unpopulated context, and
#     empty is a distinct state from both a name and the bot: `'' !=
#     'github-actions[bot]'` is TRUE, so an unknown identity TAGS rather than
#     stopping. Row 3 records that this workflow is fail-OPEN on identity. That
#     is the right posture for a tagger (a missed tag is worse than an extra
#     one) but it is a posture, and an unwritten posture is an accident.
# WHAT THIS TABLE CANNOT SEE, stated so its green is never read as broader than
# it is. `bump` RUNNING IS NOT A TAG BEING PUSHED. Everything that decides
# whether this workflow actually does its job is STEP-level and therefore below
# this linter's resolution entirely:
#   - `steps.changes.outputs.skip == 'false'` gates both "Compute next tag" and
#     "Create + push tag". A push touching only e.g. README lands here with
#     skip=true, and the run is green with no tag — the exact silent-no-op
#     shape this family exists to name, one layer down where nothing here can
#     reach it. A step-selection oracle would be needed; this is not one.
#   - the `case "$bump" in major|minor|patch|*)` dispatch inside "Compute next
#     tag" is shell, not job selection. Its arms are NOT job-visible.
# So "bump ran" means "the job was selected", never "substrate got a new tag".
# WHY ROWS 6-7 EXIST ANYWAY, and what they are honestly worth. `inputs.bump-type`
# is this workflow's only input and the first thing a reader will ask about, so
# the table answers rather than staying silent. NO `if:` READS IT TODAY — these
# two rows assert nothing about the shell `case` above and select identically to
# row 1. They are TRIPWIRES, kept for the day someone gates the job on it (the
# realistic edit: "a major bump only from workflow_dispatch"), at which point
# they diverge from row 1 and force the new gate to be written down here instead
# of acquired silently. Row 6 is the named-arm dispatch; row 7 is a value
# matching no arm, which the shell silently treats as `patch`. Row 1's empty
# value is the third state — a `push` event, where `inputs` does not exist at
# all — and it is the production path, not an edge case.
# 1. THE PRODUCTION PATH. A human pushes to main; `inputs` is absent because the
# trigger is `push`, so bump-type is empty and the shell defaults it to patch.
# The job selects. If this row ever goes NOT-RUN, substrate has stopped tagging
# and its consumers have nothing new to pin.
push-by-human
# 2. THE LOOP BRAKE. `bump` pushed the tag as github-actions[bot]; that push
# re-enters this workflow. The second pass must select NOTHING. This is the only
# row in which any job skips, and it is the whole reason the `if:` is there.
bot-actor-no-tag-loop
# 3. FAIL-OPEN ON AN UNKNOWN IDENTITY. Empty actor is a distinct state from both
# a login and the bot; `'' != 'github-actions[bot]'` is true, so the job runs.
# Pinned deliberately: this workflow tags rather than stops when it cannot tell
# who pushed, and that choice should be visible.
actor-empty-still-tags
# 4. NEAR-MISS LOGIN. `github-actions` without the `[bot]` suffix is NOT the
# actor GitHub reports for a bot push, so it must still tag. If the literal in
# the workflow is ever shortened to this form, the real bot stops matching and
# this row goes NOT-RUN — catching an unhooked loop brake at lint time instead
# of at tag v0.9999.0.
near-miss-bot-login-still-tags
# 5. A DIFFERENT BOT. dependabot[bot] pushes real changes to main and those
# changes deserve a tag: the brake is scoped to the one bot this workflow itself
# creates, not to bots as a class. Widening the guard to match any `[bot]` login
# turns this row NOT-RUN (or EVAL, since endsWith/contains are refused).
other-bot-still-tags
# 6. TRIPWIRE, asserts nothing today. workflow_dispatch with an explicit named
# arm. No `if:` reads bump-type, so this selects exactly like row 1; it exists so
# that a future job-level bump-type gate cannot land silently.
dispatch-major
# 7. TRIPWIRE, asserts nothing today. A bump-type matching no arm of the shell
# `case`, which silently falls through to `patch`. That fall-through is NOT
# job-visible and is not asserted here — the row pins only that an unrecognized
# input does not change job selection, and turns red the day it starts to.
dispatch-unrecognized-bump-type
